companies.name: IB INABATA

open_questions: Confirm specific battery materials portfolio distributed in Europe

companies.notes: Inabata & Co. (Japanese trading company) — European operations distributing specialty battery materials. Shown in pan-European panel in source image.

research.summary: Inabata Europe GmbH is the European subsidiary of Japanese trading company Inabata & Co., distributing specialty materials including high-performance polymer films (e.g. Toyobo Teonex® PEN film) used in battery pack insulation, EV motor applications, and hydrogen technologies. The company exhibits at major European trade events such as the Hydrogen Technology Expo 2026 in Hamburg. No proprietary manufacturing — primarily a distribution and trading entity covering all major European markets.

companies.name: KREMPEL
companies.notes: German company (Vaihingen an der Enz) making technical laminates, prepregs, and insulating materials including battery cell components. Shown in pan-European panel in source image.

research.summary: KREMPEL Group (Vaihingen an der Enz, Germany) is a leading manufacturer of electrical insulation materials, composites, and laminates for the electrical and electronics industries, with a growing focus on battery and e-mobility applications including battery cell insulation, busbar insulation, and energy storage systems. The company exhibited at The Battery Show Europe 2025 and offers flexible multi-layer insulation materials specifically designed for EV battery packs. KREMPEL operates multiple European production sites and has several hundred employees.

companies.name: ENNOVI
companies.notes: Global manufacturer of busbars, cell contact systems, and battery interconnects for EV battery packs. Rebranded 2023 from Metalsa's electrification components division. Shown in pan-European panel in source image.

research.summary: ENNOVI (rebranded from Interplex's e-mobility division in 2023) is a global manufacturer of battery interconnect systems, busbars, and cell contacting systems (CCS) for EV battery packs, with growing European operations. In 2025 ENNOVI signed an MOU with AKM Meadville to enhance CCS manufacturing competitiveness for European EV battery customers. The company will exhibit at The Battery Show Europe 2026 and is actively scaling its European supply chain for EV battery pack components.

companies.name: ELANTAS
companies.notes: Division of Altana AG (Hamburg). Specialty chemicals for electrical insulation including varnishes, resins, and impregnating materials used in battery cell manufacturing. Shown in pan-European panel in source image.

research.summary: ELANTAS (a division of ALTANA AG, Wesel, Germany) is a specialist in liquid insulation and protective materials for electrical and electronics industries, with seven manufacturing companies globally. For battery applications, ELANTAS provides sealants for battery cell and pack protection, conformal coatings for battery management system PCBs, and high-voltage busbar coatings — all validated to automotive standards. In 2025 ELANTAS employed approximately 1,784 people with sales of €861 million, and presented its EV battery coating portfolio at Productronica 2025; it is also investing in a new sustainable high-voltage insulation hub at Breitenbach, Switzerland.

companies.name: G-TEM

open_questions: Confirm battery cell casing product line details — G-TEM primarily known for automotive body pressings; battery case manufacture via Fuji Springs technology partnership

companies.notes: G-TEKT Europe Manufacturing (G-TEM), Japanese-owned, Gloucester Business Park since 1996. Automotive metal pressings and assemblies. Developed prismatic battery case manufacture via technology partnership with Fuji Springs (Japan).

research.summary: G-TEKT Europe Manufacturing (G-TEM) is a Japanese-owned automotive metal pressings manufacturer headquartered in Gloucester, UK, operating since 1996 with five facilities across the UK and Slovakia. The company specialises in high-precision stamped body structural components and sub-assemblies for automotive OEMs; its battery cell casing capability is reported via a technology partnership with Fuji Springs (Japan) but is not prominently highlighted in current company communications. G-TEM won the UK metal industry 'Company of the Year' award at the CBM Awards in April 2025, primarily for its core automotive pressing business.

companies.name: Avocet Battery Materials

open_questions: Confirm copper foil manufacturing timeline — European copper foil JV with Yihao New Materials and Tex Technology announced 2023; verify progress

companies.notes: Avocet Battery Materials (ABM), founded 2020 in Holmes Chapel, Cheshire. Makes battery tabs for lithium-ion cell manufacturers. European copper foil facility planned via JV with Yihao New Materials and Tex Technology.

research.summary: Avocet Battery Materials (ABM), Holmes Chapel, is Europe's only independently owned manufacturer of lead tabs for lithium-ion pouch cells, operating out of the Avocet Precision Metals group's Innovation Centre. In 2023 ABM signed a strategic MOU with NexPO (a leading Korean tab maker) for OEM tab supply to EU and US automotive and ESS customers. A separate entity, Avocet Electrofoils (AEF), plans a European copper foil manufacturing facility via JV with Yihao New Materials and Tex Technology, targeting completion by 2030.

companies.name: ADDIONICS

open_questions: Confirm commercial production status and licensing agreements

companies.notes: London-based deep-tech company developing 3D structured current collectors (Smart 3D Electrode) to improve energy density and fast-charging in lithium-ion batteries. Technology-licensing model.

research.summary: Addionics (founded 2017, London) develops 3D porous copper and aluminium current collectors designed as drop-in replacements for conventional flat foils, enabling faster charging, lower weight, and higher energy density in lithium-ion batteries. In April 2025 Avery Dennison made a Series B investment in the company, bringing manufacturing expertise. Addionics announced plans to invest $400 million in its first gigafactory (targeting 2027 opening) with additional facilities by 2032; no European gigafactory location has yet been confirmed.

research.summary: Avery Dennison Materials Europe B.V. (Oegstgeest, Netherlands) is a global specialty materials company providing a comprehensive battery portfolio spanning bonding, insulating, protecting, and tracking solutions for EV cell-to-pack design. At The Battery Show Europe 2025 the company showcased a new composite current collector (PET film with metallised copper layer as an anode foil alternative), electrical insulation wrapping films made with up to 70% post-consumer recycled PET, and RFID-based battery traceability solutions. companies.name: Solvay
companies.notes: Major Belgian chemicals group. Solef® PVDF is a leading cathode/anode binder and separator coating material for lithium-ion batteries. Expanding PVDF capacity in France, US, and China.

research.summary: Following the 2023 split of Solvay into Solvay and Syensqo, the Solef® PVDF battery binder business is now held by Syensqo (Brussels). Syensqo is expanding European PVDF capacity to 35 kt/year at its Tavaux, France plant, with completion targeted by end of 2025 and commercial operations in 2026 — making it the largest PVDF production site in Europe. In Q1 2025 Syensqo signed multi-year Solef® PVDF supply contracts with automotive OEMs and battery makers worth more than €150 million in cumulative net sales.

companies.name: ARKEMA
companies.notes: French specialty chemicals group. Kynar® PVDF is a key battery binder for cathode and anode electrodes.

research.summary: Arkema (Colombes, France) produces Kynar® PVDF — a leading electrode binder for lithium-ion battery cathodes and anodes — at its Pierre-Bénite plant in France, with additional capacity in China and the US. Arkema has announced a 50% expansion of Kynar® PVDF capacity at Pierre-Bénite to serve European battery customers; a new US plant line is set to start up in Q2 2026. The company targets €1 billion+ in battery sales by 2030 and reported around 20% PVDF demand growth in 2024 continuing into 2025, with a European market rebound noted in Q1 2025.

research.summary: Alteo (Gardanne, France) is a mid-size French specialty alumina producer supplying battery-grade alumina for separator coatings, cathode edge coatings, and NCA precursor applications. In a notable strategic development, Alteo and W-Scope (world leader in EV battery separator production) have signed an agreement to build the largest battery separator production site in Europe on or near Alteo's Gardanne site, targeting production start in 2026 and creating more than 1,000 direct jobs. Alteo has also recently invested in expanded grinding capacity at its French and Korean sites.

companies.name: ARMOR GROUP
companies.notes: French industrial group, Nantes. ARMOR's battery current collector foil business produces aluminum and copper coated films for lithium-ion battery electrodes.

research.summary: ARMOR GROUP (Nantes) operates Armor Battery Films, which manufactures En'Safe® primed aluminum and copper current collector foils for lithium-ion battery and ultracapacitor manufacturers. In September 2024 Armor Battery Films moved into a brand-new €37 million industrial site at La Chevrolière (near Nantes), with the first of three production lines operational by late 2024; the factory is designed to increase annual coating capacity fivefold to 150 million m² (equivalent to ~40 GWh). A third production line is already planned for 2026–2028.

companies.name: SENIOR

open_questions: Identify company — logo reads 'SENIOR', Eskilstuna Sweden; possible Senior plc (UK-listed, thermal management tubes for automotive/EV) or a Swedish entity

companies.notes: Logo reads 'SENIOR', Eskilstuna. Identity clarified by research: this is Shenzhen Senior Technology Material Co., Ltd. (Senior Europe), a leading Chinese battery separator film manufacturer that has invested SEK 2.5 billion (approximately €250 million) to build a major European production facility at Svista industrial estate, Eskilstuna, Sweden.

research.summary: Shenzhen Senior Technology Material Co. ('Senior Europe', Eskilstuna) is building one of Europe's largest battery separator film plants, with an investment of approximately €250 million and a target annual capacity of 600 million m² of separator film (enough for approximately 600,000 EVs). The first production lines for coating and slitting are already operational; the full 70,000 m² facility was targeted for completion by 2025 with a second factory under construction. The plant was originally intended to supply Northvolt's Skellefteå gigafactory.

companies.name: GRANGES
companies.notes: Swedish aluminum rolling company. Finspång plant produces aluminum rolled products including battery-grade aluminum foil for cathode current collectors.

research.summary: Gränges (Finspång, Sweden) is a leading European aluminum rolling company with a dedicated battery cathode foil product line at its Finspång plant. The company committed SEK 600 million (~$58 million) to double battery foil production capacity in Finspång, with the first new battery foil equipment operational in a cleanroom environment; full capacity was targeted to come online during 2025. Gränges' cathode foil features low carbon footprint, high strength, and superior elongation properties for lithium-ion battery cathode current collectors.

companies.name: ZNL ENERGY

open_questions: Confirm commercial readiness of ZNL-NPx separator — as of early 2026 described as preparing for large-scale production

companies.notes: Norwegian battery technology startup founded 2021, Bergen/Kokstad. ZNL-NPx non-porous separator eliminates thermal runaway risk in Li-ion and Na-ion batteries. Also develops zinc-ion battery cells for stationary storage. Pilot manufacturing line in Norway.

research.summary: ZNL Energy (Bergen, Norway, founded 2021) develops the ZNL-NPx non-porous fire-retardant separator for lithium-ion and sodium-ion batteries, which eliminates thermal runaway risk without relying on scarce materials. In November 2024 ZNL signed an MOU with High Performance Battery Technology GmbH (HPB, Germany) to integrate ZNL-NPx into solid-state battery systems; early validation results (3,300+ cycles at 1C) were presented in January 2025. ZNL also has an intention agreement with Narada for customer offtake equivalent to 4 GWh/year from 2025, with pilot manufacturing ongoing in Norway.

companies.name: SK IE Technology

open_questions: Confirm separator production capacity at Dąbrowa Górnicza facility

companies.notes: SK Innovation subsidiary (SKIET). European battery separator production plant in Dąbrowa Górnicza, Poland. Key global separator supplier for EV battery makers.

research.summary: SK IE Technology (SKIET), a subsidiary of SK Innovation, operates Europe's largest battery separator plant in Dąbrowa Górnicza, Poland — its first European production base. The facility is scaling from an initial 340 million m² capacity (Plant 1) toward a total of four plants with a combined capacity of approximately 1.54 billion m² per year, which is sufficient for around 2 million EVs and represents a targeted ~30% share of the European separator market by 2025. The Polish plant supplies major European battery cell customers.

companies.name: Elring Klinger
companies.notes: German automotive supplier. Makes gaskets, seals, battery housing components, and cell contact systems for EV batteries. Has expanded significantly into battery cell components and pack hardware.

research.summary: ElringKlinger (Dettingen unter Teck, Germany) is a major automotive supplier that has built a significant battery technology business, covering cell contact systems, battery housing components, and sealing solutions for EV battery packs. The company secured €33.8 million in IPCEI funding through 2026 for an innovative battery cell housing concept that reduces component count by up to 25% and cuts carbon footprint by ~40%. A large-scale series production order for cell contact systems ramped up from 2025, and its new US EV battery center also began operations in mid-2025.

companies.name: SCHLENK
companies.notes: Schlenk Metallic Pigments GmbH, Roth (Bavaria). Copper foil for anode current collectors and metal powders. Key European copper foil supplier for battery manufacturers.

research.summary: SCHLENK Metal Foils GmbH & Co. KG (Roth-Barnsdorf, Bavaria) is a key European manufacturer of rolled copper foil for lithium-ion battery anode current collectors, with proprietary high-tensile alloy (HTA-600®) foils achieving tensile strength of 500–600 MPa — approximately 50% higher than pure copper — while maintaining ~86% IACS conductivity. Foils are manufactured in thicknesses from 6 to 100 µm and widths up to 650 mm. The company also produces metallic pigments, battery tab ribbons, and specialty metal powders, and offers sample kits directly to battery cell developers.

companies.name: SCHOTT
companies.notes: Specialty glass group, Mainz. Products include glass-to-metal seals (cell terminals), glass fiber components, and specialty glass for prismatic and cylindrical battery cells.

research.summary: SCHOTT AG (Mainz, Germany) develops proprietary glass-to-metal and glass-to-aluminium sealing technology for lithium-ion battery cell lids and terminals, with hermetically sealed lid systems for cylindrical and prismatic cells rated for up to 20-year service life. SCHOTT is notably the first company to achieve a permanently tight glass-aluminium bond, replacing the conventional plastic sealing material that ages rapidly under harsh cell conditions. The company supplies GTMS (glass-to-metal seal) lid systems in standard and customised geometries, including steel, stainless steel, and aluminium variants for automotive battery cell producers.

companies.name: Nabaltec
companies.notes: Nabaltec AG, Schwandorf (Bavaria). Specialty alumina and aluminium hydroxide for battery separator coating and cathode applications.

research.summary: Nabaltec AG (Schwandorf, Bavaria) is one of the world's leading producers of boehmite-based ceramic coating material for lithium-ion battery separators, and also supplies specialty aluminas for cathode applications. The company announced a multi-million euro investment to more than double its boehmite production capacity at Schwandorf from 10,000 to 25,000 tonnes/year to meet growing Li-ion battery market demand. Additionally, Nabaltec is scaling aluminium hydroxide capacity for thermal management applications from 20,000 to 50,000 tonnes/year by mid-2025.

companies.name: PWO
companies.notes: Progress-Werk Oberkirch AG (PWO). Precision metal components for electric vehicles including battery housing and structural parts.

research.summary: PWO AG (Oberkirch, Baden-Württemberg) is a listed automotive supplier producing precision lightweight metal components via deep-drawing and stamping, with electric vehicle applications including battery housing parts, e-motor housings, and structural EV components. The company operates across Germany, Czech Republic, Mexico, Canada, and China. In the first nine months of 2025 PWO reported 'encouraging figures' and is actively pursuing new EV platform orders; it positions itself around three megatrends of electrification, safety, and comfort in the automotive sector.

The company actively participates in e-mobility trade fairs and supplies component materials to the battery cell manufacturing industry.

research.summary: GVS S.p.A. (Zola Predosa, Bologna, Italy) is a global leader in filtration and separation membranes for healthcare, life sciences, and industrial applications, including porous polymer membranes suitable for battery cell separator use. GVS produces battery separators as porous polymeric membranes to prevent anode-cathode contact, with expertise in precision membrane manufacturing. As of 2025 GVS is investing in a new Zola Predosa facility for innovative diaphragms for alkaline water electrolysis (4 GW/year electrolyser capacity), demonstrating its broader membrane technology ambitions beyond batteries.
